summary: Inference-time LLM optimization can cut API spend by 50-90% while improving latency, often reducing monthly bills from tens of thousands to a fraction of that. The highest-leverage techniques are prompt caching and semantic caching (with real-world hit rates around 68%), followed by model cascading and prompt compression. Most teams can achieve 60-80% savings by combining caching with smart model selection and prompt engineering without sacrificing output quality.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Cache the static portion of prompts (system instructions, few-shot examples, long context/documents) so providers charge a steeply discounted rate on cached input tokens instead of reprocessing them on every call.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on repeated input tokens
techniques.example: Place a large unchanging system prompt and RAG context at the start of the request and mark it with Anthropic's cache_control breakpoint so subsequent turns only pay full price for the new user message.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store prior query/response pairs with embeddings and return a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar, skipping the LLM call entirely. Real deployments see ~68% hit rates.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming FAQ-style questions; when cosine similarity to a stored question exceeds 0.95, serve the cached response instead of calling the model.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route easy requests to small/cheap models and only escalate to expensive frontier models when a confidence check or validator fails, matching model cost to task difficulty.
techniques.example: Send all queries first to GPT-4o-mini; if the response includes a low-confidence flag or fails a schema check, retry the same prompt on GPT-4o.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduce token count in prompts by removing redundancy, trimming few-shot examples, and using compression tools that drop low-information tokens from long contexts while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run long RAG context through Microsoft LLMLingua to compress it 3-5x before sending, keeping only the tokens the model needs to answer.

techniques.name: Max Output Token Limits
techniques.description: Cap the max_tokens parameter and instruct the model to be concise, since output tokens are typically 3-5x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and add 'Answer in one sentence' for classification tasks to prevent the model from generating verbose, costly completions.

techniques.name: Structured / Constrained Output
techniques.description: Use JSON mode, function calling, or grammar-constrained decoding to get compact structured responses, eliminating wordy natural-language padding and re-prompting for format fixes.
techniques.example: Request results via OpenAI structured outputs with a strict JSON schema so the model returns only the needed fields instead of an explanatory paragraph.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into a single batch job or combine several small tasks into one prompt to amortize overhead and use cheaper async batch pricing.
techniques.savings: up to 50% reduction via batch API discounts
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 non-urgent classification prompts through OpenAI's Batch API to get a 50% discount with 24-hour turnaround.

techniques.name: RAG Context Pruning
techniques.description: Retrieve and inject only the most relevant chunks (re-ranked and deduplicated) instead of stuffing large documents, directly reducing input tokens per call.
techniques.example: After vector search, apply a cross-encoder reranker and pass only the top 3 chunks instead of the top 20 to the LLM.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation early once the required answer or stop sequence is produced, avoiding paying for unnecessary trailing tokens and improving perceived latency.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '###' so the model halts immediately after the answer block instead of continuing to generate.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned Small Models for Repetitive Tasks
techniques.description: Replace large zero-shot prompts with a small fine-tuned or distilled model for high-volume narrow tasks, removing the need for long few-shot examples in every call.
techniques.example: Fine-tune GPT-4o-mini on 500 labeled examples so you can drop the 2,000-token few-shot block from every production classification request.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLM queries that stores embeddings and returns cached responses for similar prompts, reducing calls to OpenAI and other providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, self-hosted; infra costs only)

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Uses Redis vector search to cache and retrieve semantically similar LLM responses, cutting token usage and latency for repeated or similar queries.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, enterprise tiers custom

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallbacks, load balancing, and cost tracking to optimize spend and reliability.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, support, and advanced features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, rate limiting, and prompt management via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from $20/mo

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in in-memory, SQLite, Redis, and semantic caching layers plus routing abstractions to reduce redundant calls.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that reduces prompt length by up to 20x while preserving key information, lowering input token costs for long contexts.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, smart routing, fallbacks, load balancing, and cost/observability dashboards across multiple LLM providers.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API router that gives access to many models with transparent per-token pricing, automatic fallbacks, and the ability to pick cheapest providers for a model.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go with a small routing fee; no subscription required

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching for static system prompts and long RAG context to cut repeated input costs by up to 90% with minimal code changes.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to serve common/repeated queries without hitting the model.
Downgrade high-volume simple tasks from a frontier model to a cheaper small model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and only escalate on failure.
Set sensible max_tokens limits and instruct models to be concise, since output tokens cost several times more than input tokens.
Drop a gateway/proxy like LiteLLM or Helicone in front of all calls to get instant cost tracking, caching, and fallbacks.
